message: Has anyone tried using AI tools for patient triage yet?
We've been piloting an LLM-based summarisation tool for discharge letters.
The trust is cautious about data governance, so all models run locally.
New national guidance on AI-assisted diagnostics came out last week.
I demoed a chatbot to the consultant team; mixed reactions honestly.
The key issue is hallucination. Clinicians need output they can trust.
We're using retrieval-augmented generation to ground answers in local guidelines.
Anyone using ambient AI scribes in outpatient clinics?
We trialled an ambient scribe. Impressive, but it raised consent questions.
Consent and transparency are central to our deployment checklist.
Our CCIO just approved a six-month AI pilot for radiology.
The radiology AI flagged 12 incidental findings last month and all were confirmed.
Training clinicians to understand model confidence scores is underrated.
Data quality upstream is the real bottleneck, not the model.
Procurement takes 18 months, by which time the product has changed twice.
We run a 7B open-weights model on a laptop and it is good enough for note drafting.
Still copying results between the lab system and the EPR by hand every morning.
Annotation is expensive, so we're trying weak supervision.
There are real concerns about AI replacing clinical judgement.
AI should augment, not replace. That's our north star.
